name: NTPC Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest power generator: group installed capacity 91,506 MW (standalone 60,992 MW) with 36,899 MW under construction (17.3 GW coal, 3.6 GW hydro, 16.0 GW renewables via NTPC Green). Most thermal revenue is CERC-regulated: fixed charges on availability plus pass-through energy charges, with 15.5% RoE on regulated equity (Rs 92.9k cr standalone; Rs 1.22 lakh cr group). Q2 FY27: standalone revenue Rs 45,752 cr, EBITDA Rs 11,980 cr, PAT Rs 5,320 cr; consolidated PAT Rs 7,351 cr (+41%); first interim dividend Rs 3/share. Coal PLF 73.5% (66.0% LY); captive mines supply ~20% of coal. Group debt Rs 2.76 lakh cr (D/E 1.29). Mcap Rs 3.08 lakh cr, P/E 10.3, yield 2.8%. Stock -21% over 6 months, 52-week low reached in October.

revenue_mix.geography: India (states: UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, etc.)

revenue_mix.segment: Renewables, hydro, trading, consultancy and subsidiaries

exposures.mechanism: Bond-proxy: regulated equity Rs 1.22 lakh cr (consolidated) earns 15.5% CERC RoE (coal/gas), so ~60% of PAT is formula-based; P/E 10.3, dividend yield 2.8%. EV/MCap ~1.85 (debt Rs 2.76 lakh cr vs mcap Rs 3.08 lakh cr). +25bp on ~9.5% discount rate with regulated-asset duration ~9 => -2.4%; partial offset because RoE resets upward with the next control period => -2.0. Pack: no significant US-10y beta.

evidence.note: Consolidated regulated equity Rs 1,21,786 cr; long-term debt Rs 2,39,375 cr; short-term Rs 36,259 cr (Sep-26)
Mcap Rs 3,07,772 cr, P/E 10.3, div yield 2.84%

exposures.mechanism: Interest on normative debt is a CERC pass-through; exposure is short-term debt (Rs 36k cr, up from Rs 21k cr YoY), IDC on Rs 91k cr CWIP and non-regulated renewables (NGEL). +25bp on ~Rs 100k cr floating/short debt x 30% unrecovered = Rs 75 cr/yr vs consolidated PAT Rs 27.5k cr (FY26) = -0.3% x EV/MCap 1.85 => -0.6.

exposures.mechanism: Energy charge for coal stations is a pass-through under CERC regulations, so a notified-price rise is recovered with a billing lag of 1-2 months and with GCV/quality leakage. Offset: NTPC Mining (captive mines meet 19.9% of coal need; subsidiary profit Rs 285 cr in H1 vs Rs 1 cr) earns more on higher prices. Net +0.2; pack shows coal-related loadings significant only for international coal.

evidence.note: 19.86% of coal requirement met from captive mines in H1 FY27; NTPC Mining profit Rs 285 cr vs Rs 1 cr
Coal stock crisis: 96 plants critical in October (JSW call)

exposures.mechanism: NTPC is domestic-coal based, but higher seaborne coal raises exchange prices, strengthens demand for NTPC's pass-through capacity and the value of captive mines. Pack shows +2.71 per SSU (t +2.3); fundamentals support only ~+0.9: merchant/unscheduled sales ~4% of volume and mining profit effect (EBITDA +1%) x 1.85 x 0.5.

evidence.note: Pack empirical F_COAL_INTL +2.71 per SSU, t +2.3; beta 1.29

exposures.mechanism: Coal PLF 75.1% in H1 (70.5% LY; Q2 73.5% vs 66.0%) with PAF 90.3%; revenue is availability-based so only incentives, rebate/disincentive swings (Q2 disincentive Rs 187 cr vs Rs 488 cr LY) and merchant sales move. Standalone EBITDA grew 3.8% in Q2 on 11% demand growth. +3pp demand => +0.8% EBITDA x EV/MCap 1.85 x persistence 0.7 => +1.0.

evidence.note: PLF-coal 73.53% Q2 vs 66.01%; standalone EBITDA Rs 11,980 cr vs Rs 11,542 cr
